Get standardized population data

Source: R/get_pop.R
get_stdpop.Rd

Retrieves standardized population data for a specified standard from dict_maps.

Usage

get_stdpop(
  std = "wld85",
  sep_zero = NULL,
  age_breaks = NULL,
  method = c("exact", "interpolate"),
  interpolation_method = "linear"
)

Arguments

std

Character string specifying the population standard. Supported values are "cn64", "cn82", "cn2000", "wld85", "wld2000", "eur76", "eur2013", and "usa2000". Defaults to "wld85".

sep_zero

Logical value indicating whether age 0 should be treated as a separate group. Retained for compatibility; it cannot be supplied together with age_breaks.

age_breaks

Numeric vector of lower bounds for the requested age groups. It must begin at 0 and end no later than 85; the final group is open-ended. Defaults to the original 19 groups, or to 18 five-year groups when sep_zero = FALSE.

method

Method for obtaining the requested grouping. With "exact" (the default), requested groups must only combine the original standard-population groups. "interpolate" expands the standard population to single-year ages before regrouping, and should be used only when a requested boundary splits an original group.

interpolation_method

Interpolation method passed to expand_age_pop() when method = "interpolate". With "sprague", requested age groups cannot split 0–4 because the source 0 and 1–4 groups are combined before interpolation.

Value

A numeric vector containing the standardized population weights for the requested age groups, or NULL if the standard is not supported.

Details

eur2013 follows the 2013 European Standard Population. Its source separates ages 85–89, 90–94, and 95 years and over; these are combined into the final 85+ group to match the 19-group structure used by this package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  get_stdpop("cn64")
  get_stdpop("wld2000", age_breaks = c(0, 1, 15, 45, 65, 85))
} # }
